title: Best Golf Bags UK
short: Nine stand, hybrid and cart golf bags tested on the course, compared on weight, storage, waterproofing and how well they carry or sit on a trolley.
intro: A golf bag's real test is how it carries over 18 holes and how well it copes with rain, not how many pockets it lists. This guide compares bags tested by Golf Monthly's Dan Parker, who heads up their golf bag, shoe and trolley testing. Each bag is used on the course in different conditions, and some over half a dozen rounds. It covers bags for walkers who carry, players who use a trolley and those who do both.

products.name: Eclipse E1.5 Stand Bag
products.best_for: Walking golfers who want a light bag with plenty of storage
products.key_spec: 1.65kg, seven pockets, water-repellent Cordura nylon ripstop, magnetic rangefinder pocket
products.summary: Golf Monthly's top pick, rated five stars in testing: one of the lightest bags on the market at 1.65kg but far from small, with seven pockets including a full-length apparel pocket and a quick-access magnetic front pocket. Comfortable straps and hip pad and a 4-way divider protect shafts from wear, though it's only water-repellent and has no dedicated cooler pocket.
pros: Magnetic rangefinder pocket for easy access
Full-length apparel storage and comfortable padding
cons: Missing a dedicated cooler pocket for food and drink
products.search: Sun Mountain Eclipse E1.5 stand bag

products.name: Players S4 StaDry Stand Bag
products.best_for: Golfers who walk and carry as well as trolley users, wanting a waterproof, stylish bag
products.key_spec: 2.5kg, eight pockets, waterproof, nine colours, new stand system
products.summary: Golf Monthly found one of the best Titleist bags on the market, stylish and classic looking in nine colours with excellent storage, including an external water bottle pocket and a valuables pocket with a canopy that keeps the zip dry. The new stand system's legs kick out effortlessly and the padding makes it very comfortable to carry, though the front pocket zips could be improved and it's one of the most expensive bags on the market.
pros: Protects clubs and valuables against the elements
cons: Small improvements to the front pocket zips could be made
One of the most expensive golf bags on the market
products.search: Titleist Players S4 StaDry stand bag

products.name: Dri Lite Hybrid Prime Stand Bag
products.best_for: Golfers who split roughly 50/50 between carrying and using a trolley
products.key_spec: 2.9kg, seven pockets, waterproof, trolley-compatible base and detachable straps
products.summary: Golf Monthly found a hybrid that works both as a carry bag and on a trolley or push cart, with a lowered stand, trolley-compatible floor, leg lock system and easily detachable straps. Materials are premium but durable, storage is excellent and dividers use soft protective materials, but it's bulky to carry, so anyone carrying about 90% of the time should look elsewhere.
pros: Soft, protective materials on the dividers
cons: Bulky when used as a stand bag
products.search: Big Max Dri Lite Hybrid Prime stand bag

products.name: H2NO Lite VLO 14-Way Stand Bag
products.best_for: Golfers who play in all weather and use both carry and trolley
products.key_spec: 2.6kg, seven pockets, fully taped and sealed seams, fabric treated on both sides, VLO trolley zone
products.summary: Golf Monthly found exceptional waterproofing: every seam is fully taped and sealed and the fabric is water-resistant on both sides, so clubs and valuables stay dry in the harshest weather. A VLO design strengthens the area where a trolley handle attaches, and it's only 2.6kg with soft shoulder straps, though the silhouette is too large for a dedicated walking golfer and the price is punchy.
pros: Dedicated area for sitting on a trolley
Excellent padding on shoulder straps and hip pad
cons: Silhouette too large for the dedicated walking golfer
products.search: Sun Mountain H2NO Lite VLO 14-way stand bag

products.name: Moonlander Stand Bag
products.best_for: Dedicated walking golfers who want a light bag with ample storage
products.key_spec: 2kg, six pockets, four-way divider, not fully waterproof, seven colours
products.summary: Golf Monthly found an impressively light bag that doesn't compromise on storage, offering more pocket space than many rival lightweight bags, with a comfortable double strap system. The pocket layout is different but works once you're used to it, the four-way divider comfortably holds 14 clubs, and it's excellent value compared with premium lightweight bags, though it lacks a full-length apparel pocket.
pros: Spacious four-way top despite its small size

products.name: Player V Stand Bag
products.best_for: Golfers who want a luxury leather bag with a top-quality stand system
products.key_spec: 2.7kg, ten pockets, leather with chrome detail, Rotator Stand system, magnetic rangefinder pocket
products.summary: Golf Monthly tested this over half a dozen rounds and kept finding new touches of quality: soft but robust leather with chrome detailing, a magnetic rangefinder pocket, self-balancing straps and a Rotator Stand system that sits flush on any slope for stability in wind. It's on the heavy side for a carry bag and not 100% waterproof.
cons: On the heavy side for a carry bag

products.name: Aqua IPX Tour Cart Bag
products.best_for: Trolley users who want the most waterproof bag available
products.key_spec: 3.2kg, eight pockets, welded non-stitched IPX construction, waterproof cooler pocket with drainage
products.summary: Golf Monthly's top cart bag pick, made from a new IPX material, the world's first non-stitched, welded golf bag. In intense weather testing water simply ran off it, and with waterproof zips it stays dry inside, with a huge pocket volume including a cooler pocket that fits two large bottles. The IPX fabric makes pockets firm and tight to reach into, and there's a lot of writing on it.
pros: Delightful matte finish from the IPX material
Welded construction gives ultimate waterproof protection
Clever drainage on the waterproof cooler pocket
cons: New material gives little stretch to reach into bigger pockets
products.search: Big Max Aqua IPX Tour cart bag

products.name: Protekta Cart Bag
products.best_for: Trolley users who want organisation, quiet clubs and waterproofing
products.key_spec: 3.1kg, nine pockets, individual club slots (9 irons, 4 woods, putter well), fully waterproof
products.summary: Golf Monthly found the standout to be a unique divider where each club sits in its own locked slot, reducing rattle and noise. There's ample storage across nine seam-sealed pockets with easy one-hand YKK zips, plus two full-length side pockets, and it's fully waterproof, making it their top cart bag for storage, though there's no cart strap pass-through.
pros: Noise-reducing divider is great for organisation

products.name: All Elements Cart Bag
products.best_for: Golfers who want maximum functionality and long-lasting quality in a cart bag
products.key_spec: 2.5kg, 11 pockets, 15 dividers, insulated cooler pocket, water-resistant, eight colours
products.summary: Golf Monthly found functionality off the charts, with 11 pockets including two large side compartments, dedicated spaces for valuables, balls, umbrellas and drinks, and 15 dividers with an extra slot for alignment sticks. The build and zips feel very premium and testers expect it to last a lifetime, though the colour options will divide opinion and it's slightly pricier than some other Ogio bags.
pros: Eleven pockets leave nothing to chance
cons: The colour options will divide opinion

guide.q: Stand bag, cart bag or hybrid?
guide.a: A stand bag has legs and is built to be carried on your back, like the Sun Mountain Eclipse E1.5 and Ping Moonlander here. A cart bag sits on a trolley or buggy and prioritises storage, like the Motocaddy Protekta. A hybrid, such as the Big Max Dri Lite Hybrid Prime, works for both, and suits you if you split time roughly 50/50 between carrying and using a trolley.

guide.q: How light should a carry bag be?
guide.a: For a walking golfer, lighter is better: the Sun Mountain Eclipse E1.5 here weighs 1.65kg and the Ping Moonlander 2kg, while bigger hybrids like the Big Max Dri Lite Hybrid Prime reach 2.9kg. Golf Monthly notes light bags used to mean less storage, but the top picks here offer generous pockets too.

guide.q: Do I need a fully waterproof bag?
guide.a: It depends on how often you play in the rain. The Sun Mountain H2NO, Titleist StaDry and Big Max Aqua IPX here are genuinely waterproof, with taped seams or waterproof zips, while the Eclipse E1.5 is only water-repellent and the Ping Moonlander and Vessel Player V aren't fully waterproof.

Look for a full-length apparel pocket, an easy-access valuables pocket (a magnetic rangefinder pocket is handy), a cooler pocket for drinks, and a divider that protects shafts, such as the Motocaddy Protekta's individual club slots that reduce rattling. Pocket layout is a matter of taste, so it's worth checking how easily you can reach things while walking.
